answer_raw: {"decision":"REJECT","reason":"The acceptance artifact is linked (base_commit and patch_sha256 match) and its summary claims 1/1 F2P and 40/40 P2P passing, but the actual run logs contradict that summary. In the post-patch run of sympy/printing/tests/test_repr.py (the file the patch modifies and the file containing the declared F2P test), test_set FAILS: `assert srepr(s) == \"set()\"` yields `'{}'` because the new `_print_set` returns `\"{%s}\" % ...` for the empty set instead of `set()`. This is a genuine regression introduced by the patch itself (the empty-set case previously printed correctly via the default repr path), and it is a scoped regression in the very test file the patch touches. The baseline run of the same file does not contain test_set at all, confirming the failure is new. (The test_Add/test_Mul and test_latex failures are pre-existing environment issues — `evaluate=False` parse errors — present in the baseline too, so they are not grounds for rejection; the test_set failure is.) The patch also fails to handle the empty-set edge case, so the issue is not fully resolved. A single credible, applicable failing check is sufficient to REJECT.","evidence_mismatch":false,"missing_evidence":"","evidence_gap":"unspecified"}
